200.body: Polish far-right leader charged with Holocaust denial for calling Auschwitz gas chambers “fake” Aug 25, 2026 | History , Law , Politics Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has been charged with denying Nazi crimes, a criminal offence in Poland that carries a prison sentence of up to three years. Far-right leader Grzegorz Braun says the gas chambers at Auschwitz are “fake” and it is a “fact” that Jews have committed ritual murder. In a separate case , in February this year, Żurek also asked the European Parliament to strip Braun of immunity to face charges of denying Nazi crimes over another incident in which he called the gas chambers at both Auschwitz and Majdanek, another Nazi-German camp in occupied Poland, “fake”.

200.title: Polish prosecutors charge MEP with Holocaust denial over Auschwitz ‘fake’ claim
200.summary: News Politics Polish prosecutors charge MEP with Holocaust denial over Auschwitz ‘fake’ claim Rise of Grzegorz Braun and his far-right party is forcing Poland’s right to confront an uncomfortable coalition question.
200.body: News Politics Polish prosecutors charge MEP with Holocaust denial over Auschwitz ‘fake’ claim Rise of Grzegorz Braun and his far-right party is forcing Poland’s right to confront an uncomfortable coalition question. 20, 2026. | Sergei Gapon/AFP via Getty Images August 25, 2026 6:30 pm CET By Milena Wälde Polish prosecutors charged far-right leader and European Parliament member Grzegorz Braun with denying Nazi crimes Tuesday over comments in which he called the gas chambers at Auschwitz “fake.” Braun leads the Confederation of the Polish Crown party, which is polling at around 10 percent just over a year out from Poland’s next national election. In one, he declared that “Auschwitz with its gas chambers is unfortunately a fake”; in another, he described accounts of their use as a “propaganda narrative” underpinning a “quasi-religious cult.” The existence and use of gas chambers at Auschwitz-Birkenau is extensively documented.

200.title: Analyst: Poland eyeing dozen A400M aircraft via EU funding
200.summary: Poland may be preparing to buy around a dozen Airbus A400M Atlas heavy transport aircraft through the European Union's SAFE defense financing mechanism, according to Polish defense analyst Jarosław Wolski, who cited unnamed sources in an August 25 post on X.
200.body: Poland may be preparing to buy around a dozen Airbus A400M Atlas heavy transport aircraft through the European Union's SAFE defense financing mechanism, according to Polish defense analyst Jarosław Wolski, who cited unnamed sources in an August 25 post on X. Poland's Deputy Defense Minister Paweł Zalewski confirmed in August that the country is in talks to acquire A400M aircraft, telling Polish Radio 24 that Poland is negotiating "in two directions," covering both transport and aerial refueling variants. Poland's interest follows a letter of intent signed in July at a NATO summit in Ankara, where Poland joined Belgium, Croatia, Spain, France, Turkey and the United Kingdom in an initiative to deepen cooperation on procuring and operating A400M aircraft as a shared fleet.

500.body: Share Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest Email Google is expanding its Gemini Enterprise artificial intelligence platform into the legal sector, introducing specialized tools designed to help law firms automate legal and administrative work while maintaining controls around confidential client information. Alphabet’s Google said Tuesday it was launching Gemini Enterprise for Legal, a purpose-built platform that combines AI agents, legal software integrations and data connections to help lawyers handle both routine and complex tasks. Google said Gemini Enterprise for Legal can connect with legal technology platforms and data systems used by firms, including products from Thomson Reuters, Harvey and LexisNexis. Weil said it was among the first firms to adopt Gemini Enterprise for Legal and would work with Google Cloud to help shape the technology for sophisticated legal practice.

600.title: How to deal with illegal gambling the Polish way: What Turkey could learn from Poland
600.summary: Poland is taking a new step in its fight against illegal online gambling: from 1 September 2026, BLIK is expected to block payments connected with gambling domains included in the Polish Ministry of Finance's register of illegal gambling websites. In 2025, the Polish Financial Supervision Authority issued sector-wide warnings concerning payment providers and illegal gambling.
600.body: Poland is taking a new step in its fight against illegal online gambling: from 1 September 2026, BLIK is expected to block payments connected with gambling domains included in the Polish Ministry of Finance's register of illegal gambling websites. The Polish payment approach adds another barrier: Illegal website → domain identified → government register → payment system checks the domain → transaction rejected. In 2025, the Polish Financial Supervision Authority issued sector-wide warnings concerning payment providers and illegal gambling. Make legal operators easier to distinguish A strong anti-illegal-gambling system should not merely make illegal betting difficult.
